paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates. Due to the significant difference in values between high and low sparsity rates, we use the logarithmic results for comparison.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Тази стълбовидна диаграма илюстрира връзката между степента на рядкост и перплексията при два различни подхода: Per-Output и Per-Layer. Хоризонталната ос показва степени на рядкост, етикетирани от 10% до 80% на интервали от 10%, като скалата е линейна и няма отрицателни стойности. Вертикалната ос е означена като "Perplexity" и има логаритмична скала от $10^1$ до $10^3$. На диаграмата са представени две групи стълби, оцветени в синьо за Per-Output и оранжево за Per-Layer. При по-ниските степени на рядкост (от 10% до 50%), перплексията и за двата подхода е ниска и почти еднаква, като стойностите са под $10^1$. При 60% рядкост перплексията започва да се увеличава, като при 70% е около $10^2$ и достига до около $10^3$ при 80% рядкост. Няма ясно изразени последователни промени във височината при по-ниските степени на рядкост. Стойностите на перплексията се увеличават значително при по-високите степени на рядкост и за двата подхода.
model_annotations.Chinese: The graph presents a comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity values across various sparsity rates. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled with percentages ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%. The vertical axis is labeled "Perplexity" and features a logarithmic scale with values spanning from 10^1 to 10^3. The graph displays two sets of bars, colored blue and orange, representing per-output and per-layer perplexity, respectively. At the lowest sparsity rate of 10%, both blue and orange bars are approximately at 4. The bars gradually increase in height, with the blue bars reaching around 7 at 60%, and the orange bars reaching around 10 at 60%. Notably, at higher sparsity rates, the orange bars are consistently taller than the blue bars. Specifically, at 80% sparsity, the blue bar is approximately at 400 and the orange bar is approximately at 1000. The bars are arranged in order of increasing sparsity rate from left to right, with no additional visual emphasis or sorting applied.
model_annotations.English: The chart illustrates the comparison between Per-Output and Per-Layer perplexity across different sparsity rates, ranging from 10% to 80%. The horizontal axis represents the Sparsity Rate, labeled with values from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, while the vertical axis represents Perplexity on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3. The chart features grouped bars, with each group representing a specific sparsity rate and containing two bars: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate, with the Per-Output and Per-Layer bars positioned side by side for each rate. At a sparsity rate of 10%, both Per-Output and Per-Layer have a perplexity of approximately 2. As the sparsity rate increases, the perplexity for both Per-Output and Per-Layer also increases, with Per-Output and Per-Layer having perplexity values of around 3 and 3 at 60%, 13 and 5 at 70%, and 400 and 800 at 80%, respectively. The bars are sorted in ascending order by sparsity rate, and no bars are visually emphasized.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm zeigt einen Vergleich der Perplexity-Werte für zwei Ansätze, Per-Output und Per-Layer, bei verschiedenen Sparsity Rates. Die horizontale Achse stellt die Sparsity Rate in Prozent dar, während die vertikale Achse die Perplexity zeigt, die auf einer logarithmischen Skala abgebildet ist. Die Per-Output-Werte sind als blaue Balken dargestellt, während die Per-Layer-Werte orange sind. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert und weisen keine Hervorhebung auf. Die Werte auf der vertikalen Achse reichen von $10^1$ bis $10^3$. Bei einer Sparsity Rate von 10% beginnen beide Balken bei etwa 3 auf der logarithmischen Skala und steigen mit zunehmender Sparsity Rate an. Bei 80% erreichen die Balken Werte von ungefähr 600 für Per-Output und 1000 für Per-Layer.
